title: Integration by Parts

methods.name: Integration by parts
methods.summary: Trade a product for a simpler integral using \int u\,dv = uv - \int v\,du.
steps: Choose u with LIATE; everything else in the integrand, including dx, is dv.
Evaluate the new integral and add + C.

methods.name: LIATE choice of u
methods.summary: Pick u as the first type present in the order Logarithmic, Inverse trig, Algebraic, Trigonometric, Exponential.
steps: List the types of function in the integrand.
Take u as the one that comes first in LIATE.
Check that du is simpler than u.

notation.note: Write the differential with its dx; never drop it.

conventions: Choose u with the word LIATE and say so on the page.
Derivatives are written in Leibniz form, dy/dx; the course never uses f'(x).
Always write the rule as \int u\,dv = uv - \int v\,du before substituting.

pitfalls.description: Choosing u = e^x (or another low-LIATE term) so that \int v\,du is harder than \int u\,dv.
Dropping the minus sign in front of \int v\,du.

subskills.name: Choose u with LIATE
subskills.description: Pick u so that du is simpler and dv is integrable.

subskills.name: Apply the parts rule
subskills.description: Compute du and v, then assemble uv minus the integral of v du.

subskills.name: Repeat parts
subskills.description: Apply integration by parts a second time when the new integral is still a product.
